Definition: from G726; pillage (properly abstract):--extortion, ravening, spoiling.
BiblicalUsage: Harpage is plunder, extortion, the thing seized by force, and the New Testament uses it for both suffering and sin. In Hebrews 10:34 the believers took joyfully the spoiling of their goods, knowing they had a better substance in heaven, while in Luke 11:39 and Matthew 23:25 Jesus charges the Pharisees that their cups are full of ravening and wickedness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the contrast is the whole sermon: one group loses its goods and rejoices, the other fills its cup by taking, and only one of them has anything that lasts. I want to be the one who can be plundered and still be rich.
